about: Matrix Morpheus is a tight close-up of Laurence Fishburne as Morpheus from The Matrix: shaved head, small round mirrored sunglasses, black leather coat collar turned up, and a steady, unreadable expression aimed just past the camera. It is the look of a mentor about to calmly break someone's whole worldview. As a meme he almost always opens with "what if I told you", followed by a supposedly mind-blowing truth. The humor comes from that dramatic delivery being applied to something either painfully obvious or quietly devastating, so the same template can be a patronizing correction or a real reality check.
origin: The still comes from The Matrix (1999), during the scene where Morpheus explains to Neo that the world he knows is a simulation. Morpheus never actually says "what if I told you" in the film; the phrase is a fan paraphrase that became the standard caption once the image spread as an advice-animal style macro around 2012.
usage:
Use the classic split: the top box reads "what if I told you" and the bottom box delivers the revelation. The revelation can be an obvious fact someone keeps missing ("you don't have to reply-all"), a counterintuitive truth, or a gentle roast of a common habit.

It works best when the bottom line sounds simple but challenges something people take for granted. Keep the delivery deadpan; Morpheus is calm, so the caption should be too.
ideas: the bus doesn't wait if you run slower
you can leave the group chat
the referee can't hear you through the TV
